subject.title: feat(exec): verified-human instruction provenance for sensitive targets

question: What verified-human provenance contract and sensitive-target enforcement surface should OpenClaw support for exec, outbound messaging, and gateway mutations?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix creates a new security boundary plus config/API semantics; automation cannot safely choose the provenance proof model, plugin visibility rules, target matching semantics, or fallback behavior.

options.title: Core Gateway Policy
options.body: Add core-enforced sensitive-target policy with explicit config/schema, provenance propagation, and stricter approval or denial fallback at the tool/gateway boundary.

options.title: Plugin Context First
options.body: First land safe hook context such as action classification and input provenance, then let a trusted security plugin implement the policy once the SDK contract is accepted.

options.title: Fold Into Taint Umbrella
options.body: Defer this request into the broader persistent-taint and content-derived execution guardrail design so maintainers choose one unified authority model.

recommendation.title: Core Gateway Policy
recommendation.body: Add core-enforced sensitive-target policy with explicit config/schema, provenance propagation, and stricter approval or denial fallback at the tool/gateway boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is around hook contracts and exec approval policy surfaces.
